title: Prefix-merge probing: stepped rollout latency vs. quality eval & regression monitor
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need an end-to-end evaluation and monitoring plan for a proposed prefix-merge change in the KV cache layer. The change coarsens cache key granularity by merging adjacent prompt prefixes to increase cache hit rate for common conversational prefixes. Expected win is lower per-token compute and higher throughput; risk is observable quality degradation for boundary-sensitive prompts and increased context leakage across sessions.

Goals:
- Quantify latency and cost savings across realistic workloads when prefix-merge is enabled at different merge thresholds.
- Detect and quantify any quality regressions (semantic drift, hallucination, structured-output errors) tied to prefix merging.
- Produce an automated canary rollout policy with trigger thresholds and rollback actions.

What this ticket delivers:
- A reproducible eval harness that runs batched A/B evals across config axis: merge_threshold={0.00,0.25,0.50,0.75}, microbatch_size={1,4,16}, cache_ttl_seconds={30,300,3600}.
- A held-out prompt corpus composed of: 10k production-sampled prompts (mixed short/long), 2k adversarial prompts curated by QA, and 1k structured-output prompts (JSON/API-style).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1000-tokens (based on current pricing model), embedding-cosine drift (avg/95th), structured-output accuracy (exact-match), logprob delta, and hallucination rate (measured by classifier + manual spot checks).
- Grafana dashboard with real-time canary panels and automated regression alerts wired into PagerDuty and Slack.
- Canary rollout plan and automated rollback policy codified in a runbook.

Eval methodology (high level):
- Offline sweep: run the harness on trace-replayed workloads from three representative tenants (PLG webhooks, search summarization, and chat assistant) to generate latency-quality Pareto curves for each config point.
- Controlled A/B canaries: route 1% of traffic to each experimental variant concurrently for 48 hours with shadow logging of outputs.
- Focused human eval: for variants that show subtle embedding drift (>0.02 cosine drop) or structured-output errors, sample 250 responses for human review.

Pass / fail criteria for rollout (canary -> 100%):
- No variant may regress structured-output exact-match by >1.0% relative to baseline.
- Embedding cosine similarity must not drop by >0.03 average.
- Hallucination rate increase must be <= 0.5 percentage points.
- p95 latency must remain within +15% of baseline and p99 within +25%. If quality thresholds are violated, auto-roll back immediately. If latency wins exceed 20% cost reduction without quality loss, recommendation to promote.

Instrumentation and artifacts:
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/prefix-merge-probing (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/421)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12456 (prefix-merge implementation + feature flag)
- Canary routing config: https://git.internal.redwood/services/traffic-configs/prefix-merge-canary.yaml
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prefix-merge/probing-evals (panels for latency, cost, embedding drift, structured accuracy)
- Eval artifacts S3: s3://redwood-evals/prefix-merge/2026-03-10/ (raw traces, metrics CSVs, sampled outputs)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle context bleed affects multi-turn privacy-sensitive prompts. Mitigation: include a privacy-sensitive test slice and block rollout if any regression detected for that slice. Add extra TTL gating for tenant-scoped keys.
- Risk: increased microbatching interaction with merge leading to p99 spikes. Mitigation: throttled canary with p99 SLO enforced; implement backoff policy in router.
- Risk: metric noise on small tenants. Mitigation: require minimum traffic volume per tenant before promoting variant for that tenant.

Next steps / open items:
- Finalize the adversarial prompt set with QA (action: Maya to sync with QA by 2026-03-03).
- Hook the embedding-drift detector to the eval harness (action: Liam to merge eval PR and schedule nightly runs).
- Confirm alert thresholds with SRE and Observability (meeting scheduled 2026-03-05).

Notes on differences from prior batching/kvcache work:
This ticket focuses specifically on the semantic consequences of coarser cache keys rather than pure batching-packing strategies. While prior tickets swept batch/cache size tradeoffs, this combines key-granularity as a first-class axis and emphasizes structured-output and semantic drift detection rather than only token-level metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness runs end-to-end for all config combinations and produces consolidated CSVs
Grafana dashboard displays canary metrics with alert rules firing on injected regressions
Canary routing config deployed to staging and 1% production with auto-rollback logic in place
Human review samples produced for any variant exceeding drift thresholds
